block.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.mod: A cockpit panel. Install _lamps_, _buzzers_ and the _FMS_ on its 3×3 grid.
Mounts on any solid face, ceilings included. Tables side by side form one panel. On an _Avionics Computer_ it docks and joins its network with no wire.
Installs the module on the cells you aim at.
On a module, opens its settings. On a _lit lamp_, silences the buzzers. On an empty cell, opens the panel overview.
R-Click _removes_ a module. Scroll over a module to change what it shows. _Sneak_ + R-Click picks up the table with its contents.
item.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.buzz: Beeps on GPWS alerts: _fast_ for warnings, _slow_ for cautions.
Installs on one cell of the grid.
Opens its settings (_Sneak_ + R-Click while it sounds): sound on _every alert_ or only on _warnings_, and the _volume_ (heard up to 16 blocks at 100%).
R-Click the _sounding buzzer_ or a _lit lamp_ on the same panel to silence it until the next alert.
item.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.fms_: Stores _waypoints_ and points the aircraft to the active one.
Installs on a _2×3_ area of the grid.
Opens the FMS: add waypoints at your position or by coordinates, then click one to _fly direct_ to it.
Click _Link compass_ to link the first FMS Compass in your inventory.
Keeps its waypoints and linked compasses.
Points to the _active waypoint_ of a linked FMS.
Open an FMS and click _Link compass_ with this compass in your inventory.
Place it in an Aeronautics _Navigation Table_ to steer toward the waypoint. Unlimited range on the same ship, _256 blocks_ otherwise.
block.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.net: Connects a CC: Tweaked computer to the avionics _network layout_.
Joins the network through a _Wire Connector_.
Works as an _avionics_network_bridge_ peripheral. _getConnectedDevices()_ lists every device on the network. For sensor readings, use the _Avionics Computer_.
block.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.rad: Measures the _height above the ground_ below it. Works on moving aircraft.
Reads the distance from its _lens_ (bottom face) to the ground, up to _128 blocks_.
Opens the _redstone output_ settings: pick the altitude range, or send the reading over a _Redstone Link_ frequency.
Signal grows with altitude: _0_ at the low limit, _15_ at the high limit.
Works as a _radar_altimeter_ peripheral. Call _getReading()_ for the current height.
block.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.ter: Terrain Scanner
Detects _obstacles ahead_ on the side it faces, before you hit them.
When placed
Scans a _90°_ cone of nine rays in the direction of its lens, up to _128 blocks_. Can hang upside down from a ceiling.
When R-Clicked
Opens its settings: which _side of the aircraft_ it looks at, the _detection range_, or a _Redstone Link_ frequency.
Redstone output
Signal grows as obstacles get closer: _15_ at the near limit, _0_ at the far limit or with no contact.
With CC: Tweaked
Works as a _terrain_scanner_ peripheral. Call _getScan()_ for the latest contacts.
Advanced Terrain Scanner
A wider Terrain Scanner with _separate outputs_ for front, left and right.
When placed
Scans an adjustable cone from _30°_ to _180°_ with up to _81 rays_, up to _128 blocks_.
When R-Clicked
Opens its settings: aircraft side, _aperture_, and a range or _Redstone Link_ frequency for each channel.
Redstone output
Front, left and right each emit from their own face: _15_ near, _0_ far. Side channels need an aperture above _50°_.
With CC: Tweaked
Works as a _terrain_scanner_advanced_ peripheral. _setOpeningAngle()_ changes the aperture from code.
gui.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.fms.w:
%s
Click: fly direct to it (again to clear)
Right click: edit
gui.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.fms.c: The first FMS Compass in your inventory. Once linked, a Navigation Table holding it points to this FMS destination.
message.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.f: Waypoint name or coordinates are invalid.
Enable rebind confirmation before linking this Navigator to another FMS.
item.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.lamp: A cockpit warning light for the Modular Table.
Installs on one cell of the grid.
Opens its settings: choose what it _indicates_, such as a GPWS warning, a caution or a single function. The lens color follows the choice.
R-Click _acknowledges_ the alert and silences the panel's buzzers.
A wide cockpit warning light for the Modular Table.
Installs on two cells of the grid. _Scroll_ while aiming at the table to turn it upright or sideways.
Opens its settings: choose what it _indicates_, such as a GPWS warning, a caution or a single function. The lens color follows the choice.
R-Click _acknowledges_ the alert and silences the panel's buzzers.
gui.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.senso: Which side of the aircraft this scanner looks at. The Avionics Computer uses it as the scanner's role and to find the nose.
The mouse wheel adjusts it too. Shift steps by 10.
Click to choose the frequency; right click to clear it.
Click to choose which slot the next item fills; right click to clear it.
Drag an inventory item onto a slot, or click it to fill the marked slot (or the first empty one). The item is not consumed.
Total scan opening, from 30° to 180°. Side outputs are off at 50° or less.
Distance to the nearest detected obstacle, in meters (1 block = 1 m).
Output is 0 at the far limit and rises to 15 at the near limit. No contact means 0.
Any complete pair selects Redstone Link for all sectors. Unpaired sectors are off; with no complete pairs, output is local.
Altitude above terrain (AGL), in meters (1 block = 1 m).
Output rises from 0 at the lower limit to 15 at the upper limit.
Fill both slots to transmit via Redstone Link; otherwise output uses the block faces.
block.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.avi: The aircraft's brain: reads every sensor on the network and raises _GPWS alerts_.
Finds every sensor on its network and gives each a role. Its screen blinks _amber_ for cautions and _red_ for warnings.
Opens the status screen: sensors, alerts, _sensitivity_ and which functions are inhibited.
When the test button is clicked
Runs a 3-second _self-test_ with every alert on.
Works as an _avionics_computer_ peripheral with every sensor reading and alert.
gui.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.avion: Open the scanner and choose which side of the aircraft it looks at.
block.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.wir: Plugs a device into the avionics network.
Mounts on a face of a sensor, computer, bridge or table. On a plain block it works as a _junction_.
Holds up to _4_ Avionics Wires. Breaking it drops its wires.
Shows how many wires it holds and their length.
Holds an Avionics Wire along its route. Carries no data.
Mounts on floors, walls or ceilings. Click it with Avionics Wire while laying a wire to route through it.
Holds up to _3_ wires side by side. Breaking it drops the wires that pass through.
item.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.avio: Carries avionics data between devices. Hangs between _Wire Connectors_.
Click a connector, then each _Wire Support_ along the way, then another connector. A preview shows whether the next point is valid.
When Sneaking + R-Clicking in the air
Undoes the last point, or cancels the wire.
One item makes _8 blocks_ of wire. Each span reaches up to _24 blocks_.
Press _V_ to see every wire through walls, colored by network state.
Click a connector, the supports in order, then another connector. Sneak-use in the air to undo.

Wires cannot cross between a ship and the world or another ship
Wire started: click supports, then a connector

Start a wire at a Wire Connector
A point changed since you clicked it; route again
gui.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.wirin: Sneak + use with a wrench to cut
Click a support or a connector
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.ta: Measure terrain and produce redstone signals.
Install and inspect physical data wires.
Build warning panels, read the artificial horizon and navigate with waypoints.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.al: Mount the Radar Altimeter with its glass lens facing down.
It measures clearance above the surface below, not height above sea level.
Near the ground, the altitude output is weak. Moving terrain illustrates changing clearance.
Greater clearance produces a stronger signal, up to 15. This lamp illustrates the increasing output.
Right-click to set the altitude range. The output screen explains the signal at each end.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.sc: Point the nozzle at the area to watch. The basic scanner has a fixed 90° cone.
Terrain, buildings and other ships inside the cone can be detected. Your own hull is ignored.
The closer the nearest obstacle, the stronger the output, up to signal 15.
An obstacle outside the cone is not part of this reading. No detected obstacle produces no signal.
Right-click to choose warning distances. The basic scanner repeats its output on every face.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.ad: The Advanced Scanner separates Front, Left and Right relative to its nozzle.
An obstacle straight ahead drives the FRONT output on the front face.
The LEFT sector drives the left face, viewed from the scanner looking towards its scan area.
The RIGHT sector has its own output and configurable warning range.
Adjust Aperture in the screen. At 50° or less the side sectors are disabled; only Front remains.
Connect each output separately. The rear, top and bottom do not output a sector.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.ou: By default, sensors send redstone through their block faces. A nearby lamp can react directly.
Adjust both range handles. Altitude grows with height; obstacle output grows with proximity.
Choose BOTH frequency items for the channel. Picking frequencies does not consume those items.
Give a Create Redstone Link receiver the same pair. It carries the signal into your cockpit.
On the Advanced Scanner, one complete pair switches the whole sensor to Link. Set pairs for every channel you need.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.wi: Mount brass Wire Connectors on devices. Each connector joins the device behind it to the network.
Iron Wire Supports guide the route along the hull. A support alone does not connect a device.
With Avionics Wire: click the first connector, each support in order, then the final connector.
Connectors join several wires into branches. The ghost preview shows route, cost and placement problems.
While routing, sneak + use IN THE AIR undoes the last point. With only the start left, it cancels.
Keep every point in one ship, or all in the static world. Ship-to-ground wires are not supported.
Press %s for Wiring View. This follows your Controls setting.
Wiring View reveals wires through the hull. Brass means a complete network with at least two devices.
Grey means no connected partner. Red means an unloaded area or a network beyond its discovery limit.
In Wiring View, aim at a wire and sneak + right-click with a Create Wrench to cut only that wire.
Removing a support or connector removes ALL wires through it. Survival returns the wire items.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.fi: Start with a downward Radar Altimeter and an Avionics Computer joined by Avionics Wire.
Mount a Modular Table directly on the computer. It docks into the network without another wire.
Add a lamp and buzzer. Their default GPWS Caution indication responds to cautions and warnings.
During flight, approaching the ground can trigger clearance and descent warnings on the panel.
The computer operates automatically. Open its screen to choose sensitivity and inhibit individual functions.
Click the small front TEST button for a three-second self-test. No arming or individual thresholds are needed.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.ex: Add a Terrain Scanner to the avionics network. It complements the downward altimeter.
The nozzle sets the actual scan direction. Point it towards the area you want to protect.
Open the scanner and set Looks at: Front for a forward scanner. This assigns its role on the ship.
A detected obstacle can produce Terrain Ahead caution. This diorama illustrates the alert sequence.
An urgent obstacle ahead can escalate to Pull Up. React to the warning; the computer does not steer for you.
Scanners extend obstacle awareness. Basic clearance and descent protection can use the altimeter alone.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.pa: Each table has a 3 × 3 grid. Mount tables on any solid face, including walls and ceilings.
Hold a module in your MAIN hand and right-click a free footprint. Simple lamps and buzzers use one cell.
The long lamp uses two cells. Scroll while holding it and aiming at the table to rotate its preview.
A red preview means overlap or a footprint outside the panel. Invalid placement consumes no item.
Neighbouring tables on the same plane join. A module can span their shared edge if every cell is free.
Use a Create Wrench to remove a module. An FMS keeps its waypoints and compass binding in its item.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.al: GPWS Caution uses amber lamps. A buzzer set to Caution sounds for cautions and warnings.
GPWS Warning uses red lamps. A specific-function lamp changes from amber caution to red warning.
GPWS INOP means protection lacks usable data or connectivity. It does not mean the path is clear.
Right-click a lit lamp or sounding buzzer with an empty hand to silence the panel. Visual warnings remain.
A new alert or escalation reactivates sound. Silencing does not disable the computer’s protection.
Sneak + right-click opens an active module’s settings. Wrench + scroll changes indication or buzzer volume. Test before flight.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.fm: Install the FMS on a free 2 × 3 footprint. Right-click anywhere on it to open the waypoint screen.
Choose New waypoint. Use your current position or enter coordinates, name the point and confirm.
Select a waypoint to fly direct. The screen shows destination, distance and bearing; the module displays a compass.
Keep an FMS Compass in your inventory and use Bind compass in this FMS screen. It follows this exact module.
Insert the linked FMS Compass into Aeronautics’ Navigation Table. Its pointer follows the selected destination.
Selecting another waypoint redirects the table. This gives a navigation target; it does not fly the ship automatically.
Click the active waypoint again or Clear destination to remove the navigation target.
Removing and reinstalling an FMS keeps its waypoints and compass binding. Keep the FMS loaded in the same dimension.
ponder.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.at: Setting the aircraft frame
The Attitude Reference Unit reads the aircraft's own pose. The little plane inside only shows how the unit is set; its propeller is for show.
The plane's copper nose marks the Nose: the direction the unit takes as forward. A new unit faces where you were looking.
Its tail fin, with the light tip, marks Up: the direction it takes as the sky side. The stand is on the opposite face. Nose and Up are always perpendicular.
Right-click a face with a wrench to make it the Nose. The block does not turn; only the plane inside does.
Right-click for the screen and pick the Up there. A unit on its side or lying flat only needs the right pair.
Calibrate level records the current attitude as 0° pitch and roll, up to 15° per axis. Use it for an aircraft that rests tilted.
Damping smooths the published numbers: off, light or strong. The Attitude Indicator already smooths its own picture.
Wire it straight to a table, no computer needed. It publishes pitch, roll and heading to the whole network: Attitude Indicators, the GPWS bank angle and CC: Tweaked.
Off a moving aircraft the unit reports level flight. Test it on the ship, not on the ground.
Reading the artificial horizon
Put a Wire Connector on the Attitude Reference Unit and one on the table, and wire them together. The table is an endpoint of the network: no Avionics Computer is needed.
Right-click a table with the Attitude Indicator. It takes 2 × 2 cells, also across joined tables.
The display draws sky above and ground below the horizon line, with a pitch ladder and a bank scale on top.
Nose up moves the horizon down the display. The ladder marks every 5° and numbers every 10°.
Nose down moves the horizon up. The fixed aircraft symbol shows where the nose points.
The horizon and the bank scale tilt with the roll. Right wing down is positive. It keeps working inverted.
Right-click with an empty hand for the screen: live pitch and roll, the state of each source and the altitude tape.
A floor table gets a slanted housing with an upright display. A wall or ceiling table gets a flat plate.
Sources, tapes and ATT flags
The display reads the nearest Attitude Reference Unit on the table's cable network. It must be on the same aircraft as the table.
Add a Radar Altimeter to the same network and an altitude tape slides in on the right.
The tape shows clearance above the ground in blocks. With several altimeters, the lowest one wins.
Out of the radar's range the tape reads ----. The horizon never depends on the altimeter.
The screen has a switch for the altitude tape. Off, the tape slides away and the horizon grows to fill the display.
With the nose near vertical the roll is held at its last value and a small amber ATT flag appears.
With no usable unit the screen goes black with a red ATT flag. The same happens if the network is incomplete.
A unit on another aircraft, or one with no fresh reading, is ignored. The screen lists the state of each source.
aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.ponder.ta: Measure terrain and produce redstone signals.
Install and inspect physical data wires.
Build warning panels, read the artificial horizon and navigate with waypoints.
block.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.att: Reads the aircraft's _pitch_, _roll_ and _heading_ from its own pose, not from a swinging weight.
The _Nose_ faces where you look and the _Up_ faces the sky. Both can be changed later.
That face becomes the _Nose_. The _Up_ is set in the screen, and always stays perpendicular.
Opens the screen: the _Nose_ and _Up_ faces, the _level calibration_ (up to 15°) and the _damping_.
gui.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.attit: Not on a moving aircraft: reporting level flight.
The next face you pick becomes the Nose.
The next face you pick becomes the Up.
Records the current attitude as 0° pitch and roll. Valid only within 15° on each axis.
Smooths the published values. The display stays smooth on its own.
Live reading of the aircraft: pitch (nose up is positive), roll (right wing down is positive) and heading (0° north, clockwise).
Nose is the direction the unit takes as forward; Up is the direction it takes as up. They are always perpendicular. Set them here or with the wrench on a face.
Level offset. Calibrate level records the current attitude as 0° pitch and roll (up to 15° per axis); reset clears it.
Smooths the published values: off (raw), light or strong. The display stays smooth on its own.
item.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.atti: An artificial horizon for the cockpit panel. It reads the attitude of the nearest _Attitude Reference Unit_ and the height of the _Radar Altimeter_ on the same cable network and aircraft.
Takes _2×2_ cells of the grid, also across joined tables. A floor table gets a slanted housing, a wall or ceiling table a flat plate.
When R-Clicked with an empty hand
Opens the screen: the live attitude, the _sources_ it reads and the _altitude tape_.
The screen goes black with a red _ATT_ flag.
gui.aeronautics_fly_by_instruments.attit: What the display shows now: pitch (nose up is positive) and roll (right wing down is positive).
No attitude: the display shows the red ATT flag.
Nose near vertical: the roll is held at its last value.
The display reads the nearest Attitude Reference Unit, the lowest Radar Altimeter and the nearest Velocity Sensor on the table's cable network. All of them must be on the same aircraft as the table.
Tapes are drawn beside the horizon. A tape that is off gives its space back to the horizon.
Height above ground in blocks (AGL). Shown only while a Radar Altimeter is on the network.
Speed along the sensor's face, in blocks per second. Point the Velocity Sensor at the nose. Shown only while a Velocity Sensor is on the network.
